channel.title: Saurav Sana | Field Notes
channel.description: Field notes on distributed systems, queueing physics, lakehouse gateways, and software economics. Grounded in reality, skeptical of architectural dogma.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Appendix): Mapping the Shape of Failure to LLM Infrastructure
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Engineering reference matrix for LLM infrastructure: KV-cache memory accounting (2 * L * H_kv * d_h * b_bytes), operational HBM admission limits, Rogan-Gladen correction for imperfect semantic evaluators, and uncertainty propagation.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 8): The Stochastic Shape of AI Systems
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Why an HTTP 200 in 180 ms can still be a catastrophic outage. Decomposes the 5-layer AI reliability stack (Serving, Structural, Data/Retrieval, Semantic, Execution), Categorical token sampling, KV-cache preemption, and governing stochastic agents via deterministic state machines.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 7): The Architect's Reality Check
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Operational verification for distributed models. Why Kolmogorov-Smirnov vertical tests miss a 1.2% compaction stall while Anderson-Darling tail weighting catches it, Q-Q diagnostics, Page's CUSUM drift detection, and Hypergeometric finite-fleet auditing.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 6): State, Empiricism, and the Simulation Fallacy
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: State-dependent retries, Negative Binomial burstiness, and why a 10,000-run Monte Carlo loop cannot launder bad assumptions. Contrasts unbudgeted 19.9x multi-tier amplification with aggregate token-bucket limits, and provides Wilson score intervals for canary evaluations.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 5): Routing, Sharding, and Heavy-Tailed Data Skew
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Systems fail where workload skew meets a rigid partition boundary. Discrete Zipf popularity (top 1% driving 53% traffic), continuous Pareto scan cost skew (infinite variance for alpha <= 2), Cauchy ratio metrics, and defenses using singleflight coalescing and Deficit Round Robin.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 4): Aggregation and the Extreme Tail
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Why 100 parallel storage partitions each hitting a 99% SLA result in 63.4% of parent scatter-gather queries breaching their deadline. Covers order statistics of the maximum, Student's t canary inference, Extreme Value Theory, and bounded request hedging.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 3): The Physics of Time, Traffic, and Queues
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Why utilization is a steep limit rather than a target. Poisson arrival clumping, Chernoff bounds for rate-limiter burst sizing, M/M/1/K finite buffers, Erlang stages, Little's Law concurrency caps, and Kingman's heavy-traffic approximation.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 2): Reliability, Redundancy, and the Independence Delusion
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Dismantling replication theater. Distinguishes survival R(t), hazard rates lambda(t), and renewal unavailability MTTR/(MTTF+MTTR). Covers Bernoulli series risk, Binomial quorums, beta-factor common-cause floors, and synchronous AI cluster MTBF.

item.title: The Shape of Failure (Part 1): The Illusion of Determinism
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Why sample averages lie in distributed systems. Derives piecewise mixture CDFs for 85% NVMe cache hits vs. 15% cold Iceberg reads, demonstrating why the 45.3 ms mean sits in an empty desert where zero traffic lives, and how to invert quantiles to size timeouts.

item.title: Beyond the MPP Default (Part 5): Formal Verification and Invariants
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Formally verifying gateway safety and liveness invariants using TLA+ and the TLC model checker. Proving cache coherence, absence of deadlock under concurrent multi-tenant read/write transactions, and mutation testing of architectural invariants.

item.title: Beyond the MPP Default (Part 4): AST Rewrite and Row-Level Security
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Implementing zero-trust multi-tenancy at line rate. Explores AST SQL parsing and dynamic predicate injection for row-level security (RLS) and column masking before DuckDB execution, preventing tenant data leaks.

item.title: Beyond the MPP Default (Part 3): Caching and Zero-Copy Arrow Streams
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Designing a multi-tiered cache hierarchy with OpenResty/NGINX and local NVMe storage. Covers streaming query results directly to clients via zero-copy Apache Arrow Flight protocols, avoiding serialization overhead.

item.title: Beyond the MPP Default (Part 2): The Stateless DuckDB Gateway Engine
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Deep dive into embedding DuckDB workers in stateless containers. How to read Apache Iceberg metadata, hydrate column chunks from object storage, isolate tenant memory pools, and scale horizontally without cluster coordination.

item.title: Beyond the MPP Default (Part 1): Designing Data Gateway for the 95% Reality
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Architectural blueprint for turning immutable lakehouses into interactive, zero-copy operational engines for web APIs and AI agents. Why traditional distributed MPP engines incur severe structural coordination overhead on small queries, and how a stateless gateway fixes it.

item.title: The $28,500 PDF Nobody Read?
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: An empirical audit of corporate thought leadership, senior engineering opportunity costs, and why marketing whitepapers generate zero qualified leads. Evaluates the PR Decay Model of signal attenuation and vanity content pipelines.

item.title: The Flaw of Sprints
item.author: sana.saurav@gmail.com (Saurav Sana)
item.description: Why Scrum Masters need Kingman’s formula and queueing math rather than another certification. How running engineering team capacity at 100% guarantees non-linear wait-time inflation and systematic delivery failure.
